record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For brick tiling billiards in which every other row of a square tiling is shifted by a parameter theta, determine the dynamics when theta is irrational, since rational theta gives periodicity of all orbits.

evidence.quote: The behavior for θ not in Q has not yet been studied.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the tiling of the plane by unit squares arranged so that the squares in every other horizontal row are translated horizontally by a fixed parameter θ ∈ [0,1) (a "brick tiling" with offset θ). A tiling billiard trajectory is the piecewise-linear path of a point particle that travels in straight lines inside each tile and, upon crossing an edge between two adjacent tiles, refracts according to the law of negative refraction (the reflected direction is the reflection of the incoming direction across the edge being crossed, so the trajectory crosses the edge with the angle of incidence equal to the angle of refraction but on the opposite side of the normal).

It is known that when θ ∈ ℚ, every (nonsingular) trajectory of this billiard system is periodic (in fact, with a uniform bound on the period depending on the denominator of θ).

Problem: Determine the dynamical behavior of tiling billiard trajectories on the brick tiling with shift parameter θ when θ is irrational. In particular, describe whether trajectories are periodic, drift-periodic, bounded, escaping, recurrent, equidistributed, etc., and identify the underlying dynamical structure (e.g. interval exchange, rotation, or otherwise) governing their long-term behavior.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (S. Park, M.A. thesis, University of Maine, 2025) treats brick tiling billiards with rational offset p/q, proving every nonsingular trajectory is periodic or drift-periodic with period at most 4|2q−1|. No publication located that resolves the dynamics for irrational θ; the irrational case appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: General Behavior of Brick Tiling Billiards (S. Park, U. Maine thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: For rational offset p/q every nonsingular trajectory is periodic or drift-periodic with period at most 4|2q-1|; sharper bound 4q when offset is 1/q.
status_evidence.claim: The recent thesis solves the rational offset case but does not address irrational θ.

status_evidence.title: Negative refraction and tiling billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces tiling billiards via negative refraction across tile edges.
status_evidence.claim: Background defining the tiling-billiard dynamics under consideration.
